body.en:
Question B-006-008-010.

Why the correct answer is right: A trap is a parallel resonant circuit made from a coil and capacitor. In an antenna element, it can isolate or include wire sections so the antenna works on different bands.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "A large wire-wound resistor": A resistor dissipates radio-frequency (RF) power as heat; it is not a resonant circuit that isolates or connects antenna sections by frequency.
- sourceIndex 2: "A coil wrapped around a ferrite rod": A coil on ferrite is an inductor or choke by itself; without the parallel capacitor it is not the resonant trap described here.
- sourceIndex 3: "A hollow metal can": A hollow metal can might be part of a cavity or shield, but it is not the coil-and-capacitor parallel circuit used as a wire-antenna trap.
